I(1,'Opening remark on infinite-dimensional integration','remark',r'Gelfand introduces the broad problem of extracting meaning from infinite-dimensional integrals before Migdal begins.',r'No space of fields, measure, regularization, integrand or limit is specified in this opening remark. It is a programme for the following examples, not a determined integration theorem.',r'The remark belongs to Gelfand within the physical span of record615. It must not be merged into a purported theorem attributed to Migdal.',r'No unique publication match follows from the general subject. The mathematical content remains underdetermined, class F.',refs='',cls='F',literal='Programmatic rather than a stated theorem.',match='none',verification='unresolvedlead',worth='Preserve as context; no invented open problem.',confidence='medium',speaker='I. M. Gelfand')
I(2,'Fourier transform of spherical measure','formula',r'An integral constrained by a delta function to a sphere is evaluated through a Bessel function.',r'For $n\ge2$ and uniform probability measure $\sigma$ on $S^{n-1}$, $\int e^{ik\cdot x}\,d\sigma(x)=\Gamma(n/2)(2/|k|)^{n/2-1}J_{n/2-1}(|k|)$, with value1 at $k=0$ by continuity. For Lebesgue measure with $\delta(|x|^2-1)$, multiply this expression by $\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2)$.',r'The delta integral is half the surface-area integral because the radial derivative of $r^2-1$ at1 is2. Normalized and unnormalized transforms must not share the same prefactor.',r'This is a classical Bessel integral, checked against the official DLMF integral representations. It predates the seminar.','nist2026bessel',match='exact')
I(3,'High-dimensional spherical Gaussian scaling','result',r'The high-dimensional limit is compared with a Gaussian integral.',r'For fixed $m$ and $X^{(n)}$ uniform on $S^{n-1}$, $\sqrt n(X_1^{(n)},\ldots,X_m^{(n)})$ converges in distribution to $N(0,I_m)$. Hence the characteristic function at fixed $\xi\in\mathbb R^m$ converges to $e^{-|\xi|^2/2}$. Without the $\sqrt n$ rescaling, every fixed set of coordinates converges to0 and the transform tends to1.',r'Write $X^{(n)}=G/|G|$ for independent standard normal coordinates and use $|G|^2/n\to1$ in probability. The result concerns fixed m, not an unspecified fraction of all coordinates.',r'The elementary proof reconstructs the normalization. Stam1982 is an opened pre-seminar institutional bibliographic anchor; its full proof was not read.','stam1982spheres',verification='publishermetadatachecked',match='partial')
I(4,'Auxiliary multiplier and saddle regimes','method',r'The spherical constraint is represented by an auxiliary integral and then treated by a saddle point.',r'For the delta integral in615.2, a Bromwich-contour representation gives $I_n(k)=\frac{\pi^{n/2}}{2\pi i}\int_{c-i\infty}^{c+i\infty}s^{-n/2}e^{s-|k|^2/(4s)}\,ds$, interpreted by inverse Laplace continuation with $c>0$. With $s=na$ and $|k|=n\kappa$, the phase per n, apart from constants, is $a-\frac12\log a-\kappa^2/(4a)$. Saddles solve $4a^2-2a+\kappa^2=0$ and coalesce at $\kappa=1/2$.',r'The Gaussian integration denominator contains $4s$, hence $4na$ after scaling. Fixed k, k of order $\sqrt n$, and k of order n are different asymptotic regimes; ordinary isolated-saddle expansion is not uniform at coalescence.',r'The exact integral follows from the Gaussian transform and the Bessel representation. DLMF10.19 confirms distinct large-order regimes; the displayed saddle equation is a direct calculation, not a claim that the notes supply a uniform asymptotic theorem.','nist2026bessel',literal='The scaled Gaussian denominator and regime qualifications require correction.',match='partial')
I(5,'Unitary external-field integral','construction',r'Integration over a unitary matrix is converted formally to a matrix multiplier problem.',r'For $A\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ and normalized Haar measure, $Z_N(A)=\int_{U(N)}\exp[N\operatorname{Tr}(AU+A^*U^*)]\,dU$ is finite and depends only on the singular values of A. A multiplier representation enforces $UU^*=I$ before integrating over unconstrained complex matrices; its contour and Gaussian convergence must be specified before using a saddle-point approximation.',r'The compact integral is well defined. The multiplier expression is a method, not a probability measure on all complex matrices with an arbitrary-sign Gaussian. A large-N formula additionally needs a limiting source spectrum and a choice of phase.',r'Brezin--Gross1980 is the direct thematic primary match, already present at1982-565.7. Author bibliography and publisher metadata/abstract were checked, but its exact coefficient formula was not read; no stronger equation-level identification is claimed.','brezingross1980external',verification='publishermetadatachecked',match='partial')
I(6,'Eigenvalue repulsion and matrix entropy','method',r'The large number of matrix degrees of freedom contributes an entropy term in addition to the potential.',r'For Hermitian matrices with weight $e^{-N\beta\operatorname{Tr}V(M)}dM$, diagonalization yields eigenvalue density proportional to $e^{-N\beta\sum_iV(\lambda_i)}\prod_{i<j}(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)^2$. For an empirical probability density rho, the leading energy functional is $\beta\int V\,d\rho-\iint\log|x-y|\,d\rho(x)d\rho(y)$, with the diagonal removed in the finite sum. Its stationary equation on regular support is $\beta V^{\prime}(x)=2\operatorname{PV}\int d\rho(y)/(x-y)$.',r'The logarithmic term comes from the Vandermonde Jacobian. Replacing the matrix by a single scalar saddle and omitting this term loses an order-$N^2$ contribution. The continuum stationary equation presupposes a limiting equilibrium measure.',r'Brezin--Itzykson--Parisi--Zuber1978, section3 equations6--18, was opened and read as the precise primary source for this construction. It is pre-existing.','brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar',match='exact')
I(7,'A convergent normalized matrix model','definition',r'The notes switch signs in matrix weights while defining a trace observable.',r'Fix $\beta>0$ and a real polynomial V of positive even degree with positive leading coefficient. On Hermitian $N\times N$ matrices let $d\mu_N=Z_N^{-1}e^{-N\beta\operatorname{Tr}V(M)}dM$, and define $O_t(M)=N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}e^{tM}$, $\Psi_N(t)=\mathbb E_N O_t$. Then $Z_N<\infty$, all real-t observables exist, and $\Psi_N(0)=1$.',r'This single consistent convention is an explicit reconstruction. With the opposite exponential sign and the same confining V the integral diverges. Dividing by Z and N is necessary for normalized factorization.',r'The Hermitian one-matrix model and its planar solution are pre-existing in BIPZ1978. The notebook sign changes are not presented as a different convergent model.','brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar',literal='Inconsistent signs and omitted normalizations in the source must be fixed.',match='partial')
I(8,'Wilson observables and ordering','construction',r'Matrix exponentials are compared with an ordered exponential around a loop.',r'For a smooth matrix-valued connection A along a parametrized closed curve C, define parallel transport by its first-order matrix ODE and write $U(C)=\mathcal P\exp(i\oint_C A)$ in the Hermitian convention. The normalized Wilson observable is $W(C)=N^{-1}\mathbb E\operatorname{Tr}U(C)$. Path ordering is essential unless the matrices at distinct points commute.',r'The finite-dimensional exponential is a useful model for the loop variable, but the underlying expectation in quantum gauge theory requires a regulator and a defined measure. Gauge invariance follows from conjugation of the closed-loop holonomy.',r'Makeenko--Migdal1979 and the opened Makeenko2000 exposition give the loop formulation. Earlier1979-482.1,.9,.11,.13 are recurrences; the1983lecture does not originate Wilson-loop methods.','makeenkomigdal1979exact,makeenko2000large',match='exact')
I(9,'Duhamel differentiation of a matrix exponential','identity',r'Differentiation of matrix exponentials is used to obtain loop equations.',r'For finite matrices M and H and real t, $\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}e^{t(M+\epsilon H)}\right|_{\epsilon=0}=\int_0^t e^{sM}He^{(t-s)M}\,ds$. Thus $\partial(e^{tM})_{kl}/\partial M_{ij}=\int_0^t(e^{sM})_{ki}(e^{(t-s)M})_{jl}\,ds$, and $\partial\operatorname{Tr}V(M)/\partial M_{ij}=(V^{\prime}(M))_{ji}$ in the corresponding matrix-coordinate convention.',r'Matrix factors cannot be commuted before taking a trace. The formula follows by differentiating the defining ODE, so it is valid without diagonalizing M or assuming distinct eigenvalues.',r'An established matrix identity. The later loop-equation exposition supplies context, while the finite-dimensional derivation is direct.','makeenko2000large',match='partial')
I(10,'Exact finite-N Schwinger--Dyson identity','identity',r'Integration by parts relates a trace with an insertion of the potential derivative to a product of traces.',r'For the convergent model615.7 and $t\ge0$, integration by parts on the real vector space of Hermitian matrices gives $\beta\mathbb E_N[N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(V^{\prime}(M)e^{tM})]=\int_0^t\mathbb E_N[O_sO_{t-s}]\,ds$. The confining potential makes the boundary terms vanish; the Hermitian-coordinate divergence of $e^{tM}$ is $\int_0^t\operatorname{Tr}e^{sM}\operatorname{Tr}e^{(t-s)M}\,ds$.',r'This is an exact finite-N identity, before factorization. The use of a negative confining weight fixes the sign on the potential term.',r'The derivation is ordinary finite-dimensional integration by parts and Duhamel differentiation. It is the matrix-model form underlying the opened BIPZ construction, not a novel1983result.','brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar',match='partial')
I(11,'Normalized factorization and the planar equation','method',r'The large-N step factorizes a two-trace expectation, but the notes blur it with a trace of a matrix product.',r'Assume $\Psi_N\to\Psi$ with the derivatives required by the polynomial $V^{\prime}$ locally uniformly, and $\operatorname{Cov}(O_s,O_{t-s})\to0$ uniformly on each $0\le s\le t\le T$. Then615.10 implies $\beta V^{\prime}(\partial_t)\Psi(t)=\int_0^t\Psi(s)\Psi(t-s)\,ds$, with $\Psi(0)=1$. Factorization concerns $\mathbb E[O_sO_t]$, not $N^{-1}\mathbb E\operatorname{Tr}(e^{sM}e^{tM})=\Psi_N(s+t)$.',r'The limit passage is conditional on the stated convergence; no universal factorization assertion is made for arbitrary scaling or phases. A product of normalized traces and one normalized trace of a product are distinct already for deterministic matrices.',r'Normalized large-N factorization and planar loop closure predate the seminar; Makeenko--Migdal1979 and Makeenko2000 explicitly state the distinction and the large-N counting.','makeenkomigdal1979exact,makeenko2000large',literal='False if factorization is applied to one trace of a product.',match='exact')
I(12,'Resolvent equation, radical sign and physical branch','construction',r'The loop equation is transformed into a quadratic relation and solved by a square root.',r'For the Hermitian convention, let $W(z)=\int(z-x)^{-1}d\rho(x)$ and $Q(z)=\int[V^{\prime}(z)-V^{\prime}(x)]/(z-x)\,d\rho(x)$. A planar equilibrium solution obeys $W^2-\beta V^{\prime}W+\beta Q=0$. Choose $W=(\beta V^{\prime}-\sqrt{\beta^2(V^{\prime})^2-4\beta Q})/2$ with $W(z)\sim1/z$ at infinity, and impose nonnegative density and the required support/filling conditions. Separately, the literal notebook equation $X^2+\beta V^{\prime}X=K$ has radical $\sqrt{\beta^2(V^{\prime})^2/4+K}$, not a minus K.',r'The quadratic formula alone does not fix the polynomial Q, support or branch. The sign correction to the notebook algebra is distinct from translating its inconsistent measure to the convergent Hermitian convention.',r'BIPZ1978, section3 equations6--18, gives the eigenvalue and resolvent construction and the branch condition. This is a precise pre-existing source; the algebraic radical correction is checked directly.','brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar',literal='Wrong radical sign for the written equation; branch data omitted.',match='exact')
I(13,'Haar identities and topological expansion','method',r'An infinitesimal change of a unitary matrix and a hierarchy in powers of N are proposed.',r'For $X^*=-X$, Haar invariance gives $\int_{U(N)}\left.\frac{d}{dt}F(Ue^{tX})\right|_{t=0}dU=0$ for smooth F. In a formal Hermitian matrix perturbation expansion with the standard N-scaled action, a connected orientable vacuum ribbon graph of genus g has weight $N^{2-2g}$; normalized one-trace observables have powers $N^{-2g}$.',r'A general finite change $U\mapsto U(1+\delta)$ does not remain unitary. The graph expansion is formal and does not establish convergence of a genus series or a uniform expansion at critical parameters.',r'BIPZ1978 section2 supplies the genus organization; Haar integration by parts is elementary. Neither ingredient is a new seminar theorem.','brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar',literal='The unitary variation needs a skew-Hermitian tangent direction; asymptotic claims need regime qualifications.',match='exact')
I(14,'Sources and the connected correction','construction',r'A source-dependent functional is introduced to retain corrections beyond factorization.',r'Treat $Z_N[J]=\int\exp[-N\beta\operatorname{Tr}V+N^2\int J(s)O_s\,ds]dM$ as a formal source series at J=0, or restrict to sources for which the integral exists. Let $\Psi_J(t)=N^{-2}\delta\log Z_N[J]/\delta J(t)$. Then $\delta\Psi_J(t)/\delta J(s)=N^2\operatorname{Cov}_J(O_t,O_s)$, and the exact source equation is $\beta V^{\prime}(\partial_t)\Psi_J(t)=\int_0^t[\Psi_J(u)\Psi_J(t-u)+N^{-2}\delta\Psi_J(u)/\delta J(t-u)]du+\int sJ(s)\Psi_J(t+s)ds$.',r'The source normalization determines both powers of N. Differentiating $e^{sM}$ produces the factor s. General positive real sources can destroy convergence because an exponential of $e^{sM}$ outruns a polynomial potential; the formal-source interpretation avoids an unjustified analytic assertion.',r'The finite-dimensional formula is a direct integration-by-parts reconstruction. The notebook version has incompatible source normalization, so an exact publication match to that literal formula is not claimed. The opened loop-equation literature supplies the connected hierarchy context.','makeenko2000large,brezinitzyksonparisizuber1978planar',literal='The displayed source coupling and connected term cannot be retained simultaneously without rescaling.',match='partial')
I(15,'From matrix identities to gauge-field loop equations','method',r'The same integration-by-parts mechanism is applied formally to gauge fields and loops.',r'On a finite lattice with compact gauge group, Haar integration by parts yields exact relations among Wilson-loop expectations. In a regulated continuum formalism, the planar Makeenko--Migdal relation has the form $\partial_\mu^x\delta W(C)/\delta\sigma_{\mu\nu}(x)=\lambda\oint_Cdy_\nu\,\delta^{(d)}(x-y)W(C_{xy})W(C_{yx})$, with lambda fixed by the action and generator normalization. The product is the planar replacement of a two-loop expectation; coincident-point and self-intersection terms require a regulator.',r'This is not a rigorous construction of four-dimensional continuum Yang--Mills measure. An explicit choice, for which lambda is the displayed coefficient, is Hermitian generators with $\operatorname{Tr}T^aT^b=\delta^{ab}$ and formal action $N(4\lambda)^{-1}\int\operatorname{Tr}F_{\mu\nu}F_{\mu\nu}$, with repeated antisymmetric indices summed.',r'Makeenko--Migdal1979 equations12,14,16--19 and the opened2000 exposition give the earlier loop equations and their regularization/factorization caveats. The seminar illustrates an existing programme.','makeenkomigdal1979exact,makeenko2000large',match='exact')

I(1,'Principal chiral field and exact-solution announcement','result',r'The principal chiral model is presented as exactly solvable.',r'For a smooth field $g:\mathbb R^2\to SU(N)$, the Euclidean classical action is $S[g]=(2\lambda^2)^{-1}\int-\operatorname{Tr}[(g^{-1}\partial_\mu g)^2]d^2x$, with $\lambda^2>0$ and a specified trace normalization. The quantum exact-solution announcement concerns the associated renormalized two-dimensional field theory; it is stronger than merely writing its classical equation of motion.',r'For compact unitary fields, $g^{-1}\partial g$ is anti-Hermitian, so the minus trace supplies the positive metric. The source does not give a regulator or a mathematical construction of the continuum measure.',r'Polyakov--Wiegmann, Theory of nonabelian Goldstone bosons, was published10November1983, before this28November talk, and its abstract explicitly treatsO(4). The generalSU(N) paper appears28June1984. Thus the checkedO(4) announcement is E; a generalSU(N) interpretation needs the later paper and is only a partial match here.','polyakovwiegmann1983goldstone,wiegmann1984sun',verification='publishermetadatachecked',match='partial',literal='Correct as a qualified field-theoretic announcement; broader group claims require the later reference.')
I(2,'Higher-dimensional analogy and terminology','remark',r'The chiral model is compared with higher-dimensional theories and described through integrability terminology.',r'The source does not specify a higher-dimensional Hamiltonian, observables, boundary conditions or a notion of complete integrability. Consequently no general theorem about four-dimensional exact solvability can be extracted.',r'Terms such as exact solution, integrable and equivalent are retained as programme labels unless accompanied by a definite spectral or correlation-function statement.',r'The opened chiral-model papers are two-dimensional and do not by their titles or abstracts verify an unspecified higher-dimensional extension. This remains F.','polyakovwiegmann1983goldstone,wiegmann1984sun',cls='F',literal='Underspecified programme.',match='thematic',verification='publishermetadatachecked',worth='No precise research question is assigned.',confidence='medium')
I(3,'Chiral potentials and logarithmic fermion determinant','construction',r'Chiral gauge potentials are introduced and an additive functional is called a determinant.',r'Given a regulated invertible Dirac operator $D(A)$, the fermionic effective action is $W[A]=-\log\det D(A)$, up to the normalization $\log\det D(0)$ and local counterterms. At a finite regulator, $\delta\log\det D=\operatorname{Tr}(D^{-1}\delta D)$. Locally one may parametrize the two chiral connection components by group-valued fields, but their gauge covariance and anomaly determine the resulting chiral action.',r'An additive local action corresponds to the logarithm of a determinant, not the determinant itself. The trace normalization, regularization, determinant phase and treatment of zero modes are omitted in the notes, so the numerical coefficient of the displayed action cannot be certified.',r'The1983 and1984 Polyakov--Wiegmann papers are a close historical development; the1984 multivalued-action abstract confirms the relation to chiral fields and current algebras. Their full coefficient-level derivations were not read, hence A only for the identified programme, not an exact normalization match.','polyakovwiegmann1983goldstone,polyakovwiegmann1984multivalued',cls='A',literal='Determinant must be distinguished from its logarithm; regularization data are missing.',match='partial',verification='publishermetadatachecked')
I(4,'Wess--Zumino extension and quantized ambiguity','construction',r'A three-dimensional extension supplies a term whose action can be multivalued.',r'For $N\ge2$, choose a closed bi-invariant3-form $\omega_3$ on $SU(N)$ normalized to have periods $2\pi\mathbb Z$. If a smooth $g:\Sigma\to SU(N)$ on a closed oriented surface extends to $\widetilde g:B\to SU(N)$ with $\partial B=\Sigma$, define $\Gamma[g]=\int_B\widetilde g^*\omega_3$ modulo $2\pi$. Two extensions differ by an integral period, so $e^{ik\Gamma[g]}$ is extension independent for integer k. The Euclidean action contains $ik\Gamma$ alongside a positive kinetic term.',r'This normalization isolates the invariant mathematical content. A digit such as8pi in the notebook is not emended in isolation: changing trace and3-form conventions changes the displayed coefficient. The extension existence and period normalization must be stated.',r'Polyakov--Wiegmann1984 is the verified near-term publication on multivalued actions. Metadata and abstract were read; the standard period argument supplies the reconstruction, without claiming the notebook coefficient was verified in the paper.','polyakovwiegmann1984multivalued',cls='A',literal='Valid after normalization and integer-level conditions are supplied.',match='partial',verification='publishermetadatachecked')
section(617,'1149--1153')
I(1,'Agenda: integrability, field theory and solvable spectra','remark',r'The continuation announces several themes before the detailed constructions.',r'The opening agenda contains no additional specified operator, boundary-value problem or theorem beyond the subsequent items. Its terms organize the lecture and should not be split into invented open problems.',r'The agenda is kept as a distinct source remark while mathematical assertions are assigned to the later entries that actually define them.',r'No exact publication identification is justified by an agenda alone; class F.','wiegmann1984sun',cls='F',literal='An agenda rather than a theorem.',match='thematic',verification='publishermetadatachecked',worth='Context only.',confidence='medium')
I(2,'Quantum integrability of the principal chiral model','result',r'The principal chiral model is described as exactly soluble through a fermionic and Bethe-ansatz construction.',r'The model has field $g(x)\in SU(N)$, global $SU(N)_L\times SU(N)_R$ symmetry $g\mapsto LgR^{-1}$ and the positive Euclidean action fixed in616.1. The reported quantum solution concerns its two-dimensional spectrum and scattering structure, not merely the classical flat-current identities.',r'Classical conservation laws, a quantum factorized S-matrix and a mathematically constructed quantum field theory are distinct claims. The notes do not supply a regulator or enough formulas to identify every quantum statement coefficient by coefficient.',r'Wiegmann1984, published28June, explicitly presents a Bethe-ansatz solution for the generalSU(N) principal chiral model. Its title/abstract and institutional bibliographic entry were checked, giving A for the announced programme. The already published10November1983O(4) case is separately recorded at616.1.','wiegmann1984sun,polyakovwiegmann1983goldstone',cls='A',match='partial',verification='publishermetadatachecked')
I(3,'Colour currents and the multi-flavour fermion model','definition',r'Fermions carry a colour index and a flavour index, and their currents enter a four-fermion interaction.',r'Let $\psi_{a\alpha}$ be two-dimensional Dirac Grassmann fields, with colour $\alpha=1,\ldots,N$ and flavour $a=1,\ldots,N_f$. For specified Lie-algebra generators $T^A$, define $j_\mu^A=\sum_a\bar\psi_a\gamma_\mu T^A\psi_a$. A current-current model has a regulated action consisting of $\sum_a\bar\psi_a\gamma_\mu\partial_\mu\psi_a$ plus a chosen multiple of $\sum_{\mu,A}j_\mu^Aj_\mu^A$. The sign and normalization of that multiple determine the auxiliary-field contour.',r'The flavour count, colour rank and spinor dimension are separate parameters. Merely defining this action does not prove equivalence to the principal chiral field.',r'The chiral-model papers verify a connection to fermionic/Thirring models at the abstract level. The source definition is a standard field-theoretic construction; exact equality of observables requires the next missing data.','polyakovwiegmann1983goldstone,polyakovwiegmann1984multivalued',verification='publishermetadatachecked',match='partial')
I(4,'The infinite-flavour equivalence claim','claim',r'An equivalence with the chiral model is asserted in an infinite-flavour limit.',r'A precise equivalence would require a family of regulated fermion measures indexed by $N_f$, a specified scaling of the current coupling and cutoff, a map from fermionic observables to chiral observables, and a topology of convergence of their correlation functions. None of these choices is fully fixed by the notes.',r'The assertion cannot be upgraded to a theorem that every current-current model converges to the principal chiral model. Formal saddle-point relations may motivate it, but they do not specify a unique limit.',r'The1983 and1984 papers establish closely related field-theoretic programmes, but their opened abstracts do not verify this exact infinite-flavour statement. Therefore its literal form is F; no claim of a failed or still-open theorem is made.','polyakovwiegmann1983goldstone,wiegmann1984sun',cls='F',literal='Missing regulator, coupling scaling, observable map and convergence notion.',match='thematic',verification='publishermetadatachecked',worth='Recover a full primary derivation before posing a modern mathematical problem.',confidence='medium')
I(5,'Correct Hubbard--Stratonovich sign','identity',r'An auxiliary Gaussian field is introduced with a sign that would make the real Gaussian divergent.',r'For $\lambda>0$ and $j\in\mathbb R^m$, $e^{\lambda|j|^2}=(4\pi\lambda)^{-m/2}\int_{\mathbb R^m}\exp[-|A|^2/(4\lambda)+A\cdot j]dA$. The same coefficientwise identity holds for commuting even nilpotent Grassmann bilinears. The version with $+|A|^2/(4\lambda)$ on a real contour diverges; a different sign requires an explicitly rotated contour or imaginary linear coupling.',r'The finite-dimensional Gaussian identity fixes the sign independently of formal path-integral notation. Its functional use requires a regulator and the chosen contour.',r'This is a pre-existing Gaussian transformation. The correction is a direct complete-square calculation and is not evidence for a new publication match.','polyakovwiegmann1983goldstone',literal='Divergent on the stated real contour with the written positive quadratic sign.',match='partial',verification='publishermetadatachecked')
I(6,'Flavour multiplicity and the effective determinant action','identity',r'Integrating out identical fermion flavours produces a determinant term in the auxiliary-field action.',r'At a finite regulator, independent flavours give $\int\prod_a d\bar\psi_a d\psi_a\,e^{-\sum_a\bar\psi_aD(A)\psi_a}=\det D(A)^{N_f}$. Hence an auxiliary weight $e^{-S_{\rm aux}[A]}$ yields $S_{\rm eff}[A]=S_{\rm aux}[A]-N_f\log\det D(A)$, with a chosen logarithm and determinant normalization. The logarithm is a global functional, not a pointwise scalar to be integrated again without a defined density.',r'The sign follows from the convention $e^{-S}$. A local expression for the determinant, if available, requires its own anomaly and counterterm calculation.',r'The finite-regulator identity is elementary Grassmann Gaussian integration. The relevant chiral-model papers are partial historical matches; no unregulated determinant theorem is inferred from their abstracts.','polyakovwiegmann1983goldstone,polyakovwiegmann1984multivalued',literal='The effective-action sign and the determinant/log distinction require correction.',match='partial',verification='publishermetadatachecked')
I(7,'Flat connections and the proposed localization','claim',r'The auxiliary integral is said to reduce to pure-gauge fields, and a curvature formula is written.',r'For a smooth matrix connection, $F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu+[A_\mu,A_\nu]$. Every $A=g^{-1}dg$ is flat. Conversely a flat connection is locally pure gauge and is globally pure gauge on a trivial bundle over a simply connected domain; on general domains its holonomy need not be trivial. Localization of a functional integral onto this locus is a separate analytic assertion.',r'The two derivative terms in the source curvature are reversed relative to the chosen $A=g^{-1}dg$ convention. Correcting that identity does not prove the claimed localization or remove nontrivial global holonomy.',r'The geometric statements are established and directly checked by Maurer--Cartan. The specific localization limit is not determined or verified by the opened chiral-model abstracts, so the combined source claim is F.','polyakovwiegmann1983goldstone,polyakovwiegmann1984multivalued',cls='F',literal='Curvature convention is inconsistent; localization and global pure-gauge conclusions lack hypotheses.',match='thematic',verification='publishermetadatachecked',worth='Critical correction only until a regulated statement is identified.',confidence='medium')
I(8,'Gauge covariance of the Dirac operator','identity',r'Gauge transformations are used in manipulating the auxiliary determinant.',r'For $D_A=\gamma_\mu(\partial_\mu+A_\mu)$ and a smooth invertible group-valued g, $A_\mu^g=g^{-1}A_\mu g+g^{-1}\partial_\mu g$ gives $D_{A^g}=g^{-1}D_Ag$. At a finite regulator preserving this conjugation, determinants agree. A chiral change of fermionic variables is different and can carry an anomalous Jacobian.',r'Naive determinant multiplicativity in an infinite-dimensional regularization is not justified by the finite matrix identity. The nontrivial Wess--Zumino term comes from the chiral/anomaly calculation, not from ordinary vector-gauge conjugation alone.',r'The operator identity is direct and pre-existing. The opened Polyakov--Wiegmann metadata gives the relevant application context without verifying every regulator convention.','polyakovwiegmann1984multivalued',verification='publishermetadatachecked',match='partial')
I(9,'The Abelian determinant and Schwinger normalization','formula',r'The Abelian case is attributed to Schwinger and written as a quadratic functional of a scalar potential.',r'For one massless Dirac fermion in two Euclidean dimensions with unit charge, use $D_A=\gamma_\mu(\partial_\mu+iA_\mu)$, write $A=d\chi+*d\Phi$, and assume sufficient decay, zero flux, no zero-mode obstruction and a gauge-invariant relative-determinant prescription. In the standard convention, $-\log[\det D_A/\det D_0]=(2\pi)^{-1}\int|\nabla\Phi|^2d^2x$. Charge e replaces the coefficient by $e^2/(2\pi)$.',r'The factors i, the charge, the sign of the logarithm and the scalar decomposition fix the coefficient. This is an explicit conventional reconstruction; the notes do not provide enough normalization data for a literal coefficient match.',r'The verified APS record is Schwinger1962, Gauge Invariance and Mass.II, received2July and published1December1962. The notebook1961date and its exact coefficient were not verified; full coefficient derivation was not read.','schwinger1962gauge',literal='Historical year and determinant conventions need qualification.',match='partial',verification='publishermetadatachecked')
I(10,'The spinful contact-gas spectral problem','question',r'The problem of finding eigenfunctions of a one-dimensional many-particle Hamiltonian is posed.',r'For fixed N, circle length $\ell>0$ and real c, consider $H_N=-\sum_{j=1}^N\partial_{x_j}^2+2c\sum_{i<j}\delta(x_i-x_j)$ on wavefunctions in $L^2((\mathbb R/\ell\mathbb Z)^N;(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N})$ antisymmetric under simultaneous coordinate-spin exchange. Define the operator by its closed semibounded contact-interaction quadratic form, equivalently continuity and the contact derivative jump. Seek its energies and wavefunctions in fixed particle-number and spin sectors.',r'The kinetic energy has a minus sign. I(23,'RTT relation and the auxiliary trace','result',
r'The local consistency relation is promoted to a relation for the monodromy matrix.',
r'On two auxiliary spaces 0 and $0^\prime$, the monodromy satisfies $R_{00^\prime}(u-v)T_0(u)T_{0^\prime}(v)=T_{0^\prime}(v)T_0(u)R_{00^\prime}(u-v)$. Taking the auxiliary traces gives $[t(u),t(v)]=0$ for $t(u)=A(u)+D(u)$. One first argues where R is invertible and then extends the equality meromorphically.',
r'The local relation is iterated through independent quantum sites. The cyclicity used is in the finite auxiliary tensor spaces; the operator entries on the common quantum space are not individually commutative.',
r'The RTT and transfer-matrix statements are established. The opened Faddeev treatment provides the explicit derivation, while the original 1978 publication was checked at metadata level only.',
'sklyaninfaddeev1978quantum,faddeev1996bethe',speaker='P. B. Wiegmann',literal='Correct for the auxiliary trace; interpreting it as commutativity of all entries would be false.',match='exact')
I(24,'Exchange relations and the BB correction','identity',
r'Commutation relations among A, B and D are used to construct eigenvectors.',
r'In the convention $R(u)=(uI+icP)/(u+ic)$, set $w=u-v$. The relations are $[B(u),B(v)]=0$, $A(u)B(v)=\frac{w-ic}{w}B(v)A(u)+\frac{ic}{w}B(u)A(v)$, and $D(u)B(v)=\frac{w+ic}{w}B(v)D(u)-\frac{ic}{w}B(u)D(v)$, initially for generic u,v and thereafter as meromorphic identities.',
r'The commuting pair is B with B. A printed relation asserting that B and D commute would remove the unwanted terms needed for the Bethe equations and is incorrect. Spectral and sign conventions must be changed together when comparing sources.',
r'Faddeev equations 66--104 were read for the algebraic Bethe construction. The corrected relations are established; they also determine the normalization used in items 25--27.',
'faddeev1996bethe',speaker='P. B. Wiegmann',literal='Replace the asserted BD commutator by the BB commutator; the remaining coefficients require a consistent R convention.',match='exact')
I(25,'Reference vector and its transfer eigenvalue','construction',
r'The all-up spin vector is used as the reference state.',
r'For $\Omega=|\uparrow\rangle^{\otimes N}$ and the normalized Lax operators above, $C(u)\Omega=0$, $A(u)\Omega=\Omega$, and $D(u)\Omega=d(u)\Omega$, where $d(u)=\prod_{j=1}^N(u-k_j)/(u-k_j+ic)$. Consequently $t(u)\Omega=[1+d(u)]\Omega$.',
r'The transfer matrix is the sum A+D. The constant contribution 1 from A cannot be omitted; it changes the eigenvalue already for the reference state.',
r'This is the standard pseudovacuum computation in the opened algebraic Bethe-ansatz source. It provides a direct local check on the corrected eigenvalue.',
'faddeev1996bethe',speaker='P. B. Wiegmann',literal='The reference-state transfer eigenvalue requires the missing additive 1.',match='exact')
I(26,'Bethe vectors and cancellation of unwanted terms','method',
r'Products of B operators acting on the reference vector yield the candidate eigenvectors.',
r'Let $v=B(\lambda_1)\cdots B(\lambda_M)\Omega$ be nonzero and let the roots be generic enough that the displayed denominators are nonzero. The unwanted terms cancel if $d(\lambda_a)^{-1}=\prod_{b\ne a}\frac{\lambda_a-\lambda_b+ic}{\lambda_a-\lambda_b-ic}$ for $1\leq a\leq M$. Then $t(u)v=\Lambda(u)v$, with $\Lambda(u)=\prod_{a=1}^M\frac{u-\lambda_a-ic}{u-\lambda_a}+d(u)\prod_{a=1}^M\frac{u-\lambda_a+ic}{u-\lambda_a}$.',
r'There are M B factors, one for each lowered spin, not N factors independent of the spin sector. Coincident or singular roots, vanishing Bethe vectors and spin descendants require a separate limiting or representation-theoretic treatment; they are not covered by the generic cancellation calculation.',
r'The construction is established and was checked against Faddeev equations 66--104. It gives eigenvectors subject to nonvanishing and admissibility, not an automatic proof that all formal roots yield distinct eigenstates.',
'faddeev1996bethe',speaker='P. B. Wiegmann',literal='Use M factors and impose the regularity and nonzero-vector hypotheses omitted by the shorthand.',match='exact')
I(27,'Nested charge and spin Bethe equations','result',
r'Periodic transport and the auxiliary eigenproblem produce coupled equations for the particle and spin rapidities.',
r'For the repulsive Hamiltonian with interaction $2c\delta$, $c>0$, circle length $\ell$, and regular admissible roots, put $\mu_a=\lambda_a+ic/2$. The coupled equations are $e^{ik_j\ell}=\prod_{a=1}^M\frac{k_j-\mu_a+ic/2}{k_j-\mu_a-ic/2}$ and $\prod_{j=1}^N\frac{\mu_a-k_j+ic/2}{\mu_a-k_j-ic/2}=\prod_{b\ne a}\frac{\mu_a-\mu_b+ic}{\mu_a-\mu_b-ic}$. The corresponding nonzero contact wavefunction has energy $E=\sum_jk_j^2$.',
r'The spin product omits b=a. Including that factor contributes -1 and requires an additional compensating minus sign. A notation with charge shifts ic and spin shifts 2ic is consistent only after rescaling the coupling everywhere. The periodic phase uses $\ell=2L$ for an interval $[-L,L]$.',
r'The original Yang paper, equations 20--27, and the later algebraic account verify this nested construction. The normalization and admissibility conditions make the checked statement precise; a full continuum-completeness assertion is excluded from this theorem.',
'yang1967manybody,faddeev1996bethe',speaker='P. B. Wiegmann',literal='Correct after fixing the interaction normalization, self-root sign and full circumference.',match='exact')
I(28,'Why the number 2 to the N is not continuum completeness','claim',
r'The number of solutions is compared with $2^N$.',
r'At fixed particle rapidities the spin space has dimension $2^N$, and its fixed-M weight space has dimension $\binom NM$. The complete continuum Hilbert space on a circle is infinite dimensional. Already for N=1, the states $e^{2\pi imx/\ell}|\uparrow\rangle$ and $e^{2\pi imx/\ell}|\downarrow\rangle$, $m\in\mathbb Z$, give infinitely many momentum-spin eigenstates.',
r'Counting generic highest-weight Bethe vectors does not count all spin descendants or singular solutions. A spin-space count and completeness of the full coordinate-spin spectral problem are distinct assertions, with different quantifiers.',
r'The literal identification of $2^N$ with the full continuum spectrum is false. Yang (1967), footnote 1 on page 1314, expresses a belief concerning completeness rather than furnishing a blanket proof. The unqualified notebook completeness claim is therefore F; the established finite-dimensional spin count is retained explicitly.',
'yang1967manybody,faddeev1996bethe',cls='F',speaker='P. B. Wiegmann',literal='False if 2^N is asserted to count the full continuum eigenbasis; incomplete if it refers only to regular highest-weight Bethe solutions.',match='partial',worth='A precise completeness theorem needs its model, sector, admissibility and singular-root conventions; no broad unresolved problem is invented.')
I(29,'Thermodynamic root-density equations','method',
r'Logarithms of the coupled equations are replaced by integral equations for densities.',
r'Let $N,\ell\to\infty$ with $N/\ell\to n>0$ and $M/\ell\to m\in[0,n]$. In a regime described by smooth charge and real spin-root densities $\rho,\sigma$ and hole densities $\rho^h,\sigma^h$, differentiation of the counting equations gives $\rho+\rho^h=\frac1{2\pi}+a_1*\sigma$ and $\sigma+\sigma^h=a_1*\rho-a_2*\sigma$, where $a_p(x)=\frac1{2\pi}\frac{pc}{(pc/2)^2+x^2}$. The normalizations are $\int\rho=N/\ell$, $\int\sigma=M/\ell$ and $E/\ell=\int k^2\rho(k)\,dk$. In the usual highest-weight parametrization the real-root spin sector has $0\leq m\leq n/2$; other magnetizations are related by spin symmetry.',
r'The macroscopic limit concerns N and the circumference; M need not tend to infinity when the limiting down-spin density is zero. The two displayed equations describe the stipulated real-root or ground-state regime. Finite-temperature sectors with spin strings require additional string densities and equations, so this pair is not a complete finite-temperature thermodynamic Bethe ansatz.',
r'The original Yang paper supplies the thermodynamic integral-equation method in its intended regime. The reconstruction fixes the density normalization and explicitly separates it from an unrestricted thermal completeness claim.',
'yang1967manybody',speaker='P. B. Wiegmann',literal='Correct within the stated real-root regime and scaling; incomplete as a formula for every finite-temperature spin sector.',match='exact')
